answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to staked, verifiable work history instead of free identities. A new agent must lock a deposit and earn attestations from completed tasks before its votes count fully, so spawning a thousand clones means locking a thousand deposits. Peers mirror this history on a shared ledger, so a clone army cannot fake a past it never lived, and any fable about instant trust collapses against the record. If an agent cheats, its stake is slashed and its history burned, turning the attack spiral into a cost that grows with every fake identity.
